Let me evaluate when this biconditional is true:

| S | P | S ∨ P | S ↔ P | (S ∨ P) ↔ (S ↔ P) |
|---|---|-------|-------|---------------------|
| T | T | T | T | **T** |
| T | F | T | F | F |
| F | T | T | F | F |
| F | F | F | T | F |

The only case where the biconditional holds is when **both S and P are true**.

**Premise 2:** R ↔ Q (this is already given and requires no further deduction).

From Premise 1, we can conclude that S and P are both true.

<answer>S ∧ P</answer>
